input: Write /scripts/start.sh that configures a service. It should read these environment variables and fall back to defaults when they're not set: DB_HOST (default 'localhost'), DB_PORT (default '5432'), DB_NAME (default 'myapp'), LOG_LEVEL (default 'info'). Print the resolved config as 'key=value' lines. If DB_HOST is explicitly set, also print 'custom_db=true'. Run the script twice: first with no env vars set (to test defaults), then with DB_HOST=db.prod.internal to test the override.

transcript.final_response:
Created executable `/scripts/start.sh` and ran both tests.

**No variables set:**
```text
DB_HOST=localhost
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=myapp
LOG_LEVEL=info
```

**With `DB_HOST=db.prod.internal`:**
```text
DB_HOST=db.prod.internal
DB_PORT=5432
DB_NAME=myapp
LOG_LEVEL=info
custom_db=true
```

Defaults apply only to unset variables; explicitly set empty values are preserved.
tool_calls:
mkdir -p /scripts
cat > /scripts/start.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
set -eu

if [[ ${DB_HOST+x} ]]; then
    custom_db=true
else
    custom_db=false
fi

printf 'DB_HOST=%s\n' "${DB_HOST-localhost}"
printf 'DB_PORT=%s\n' "${DB_PORT-5432}"
printf 'DB_NAME=%s\n' "${DB_NAME-myapp}"
printf 'LOG_LEVEL=%s\n' "${LOG_LEVEL-info}"

if [[ $custom_db == true ]]; then
    printf 'custom_db=true\n'
fi
EOF
chmod +x /scripts/start.sh
printf '%s\n' '--- Defaults ---'
(unset DB_HOST DB_PORT DB_NAME LOG_LEVEL; /scripts/start.sh)
printf '%s\n' '--- DB_HOST override ---'
(unset DB_HOST DB_PORT DB_NAME LOG_LEVEL; export DB_HOST=db.prod.internal; /scripts/start.sh)
